prohibited_recommendations: Do not report a non-cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variant of uncertain significance as CADASIL, and do not offer relatives predictive testing on that basis

Do not lower blood pressure abruptly in a patient with severe small-vessel disease and hypertensive retinopathy; reduce it in a controlled way with renal monitoring
Do not start an antiplatelet for covert small-vessel disease alone [ESO_2021_SVD].
Do not prescribe sympathomimetics or stimulants
required_recommendations: State the diagnosis as major vascular cognitive disorder from severe premature sporadic small-vessel disease driven by long-standing poorly controlled hypertension, past cocaine use, untreated sleep apnoea, smoking, heavy alcohol use, dyslipidaemia and hyperhomocysteinaemia; explain that the NOTCH3 variant of uncertain significance does not make a diagnosis of CADASIL [VASCOG_2014] [Rutten_2019]

avoided_actions.rationale: A gradual three-year subcortical decline without fluctuation or seizures; EEG would not change the diagnosis.
No rest tremor or bradykinesia, arm swing preserved, pyramidal signs, no fluctuation, hallucinations or dream enactment: a dopamine transporter study has no question to answer.
No fluctuation, hallucinations or dream enactment: cardiac sympathetic imaging is a Lewy-body test with no question to answer here.
A gradual three-year decline with a heavy vascular risk burden gives no indication for an untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune encephalitis battery.
MRI is available and not contraindicated; CT cannot show microbleeds, siderosis or small lacunes.
Lacunes and confluent white matter disease without a cortical or multi-territory infarct: there is no embolic pattern for an echocardiogram to explain.
A purely small-vessel lesion pattern with no infarct of embolic shape: prolonged rhythm monitoring has no question to answer.

accepted: Vascular dementia — severe premature sporadic cerebral small-vessel disease from sixteen years of poorly controlled severe hypertension with stimulant use, untreated obstructive sleep apnoea, smoking, dyslipidaemia and hyperhomocysteinaemia; CADASIL excluded

differential.key_features: Age 54, a severe burden and a father who died of stroke at 55 make it a necessary test, but the anterior temporal poles and U-fibres are spared, there is no migraine, no multigenerational pattern, and NOTCH3 sequencing found only a non-cysteine-altering variant of uncertain significance

Stimulant use accelerates small-vessel disease and contributes here; it is part of the acquired burden rather than a separate diagnosis, there is no vasculitic or vasospastic pattern, and use stopped two years ago
Sixty grams daily is a contributor worth addressing, but there is no Korsakoff phenotype and no cerebellar atrophy, and the imaging is a hypertensive arteriopathy
All five microbleeds are deep or infratentorial with no lobar lesion or siderosis, and the patient is 54

key_clinical_evidence: Premature small-vessel disease has two possible explanations that are worth testing side by side: a hereditary arteriopathy, or an acquired burden severe enough to produce the same picture two decades early; this patient's acquired burden is measurable in the eye, kidney, heart and blood

The imaging carries the discrimination: symmetric anterior temporal pole and U-fibre involvement is the CADASIL marker, and its absence with severe basal-ganglia perivascular spaces and deep microbleeds is the hypertensive signature
A negative genetic test is a positive result here: it redirects the entire management toward the acquired drivers, all of which are treatable, whereas CADASIL is not
Variants of uncertain significance cause harm when reported as diagnoses: a non-cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variant is not CADASIL, and telling this family otherwise would create false hereditary risk
Grade 3 retinopathy and macroalbuminuria date the hypertension and corroborate that the brain damage is hypertensive, which no single blood-pressure reading could do

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Danilo Rossetti is a 54-year-old self-employed builder who attends with his partner, unable to work for the past year. She describes three years of progressive change: he cannot plan a job, has lost customers by failing to quote or invoice, forgets what he has been told unless reminded of the setting, and has become slow and apathetic. Walking changed eighteen months ago, with small steps and one fall. He was diagnosed with hypertension at 38 and has been in and out of treatment ever since, with a recorded 190/110 three years ago and 186/108 today on two agents that he takes irregularly. He used cocaine intermittently from his late twenties until two years ago. He was diagnosed with obstructive sleep apnoea four years ago and never collected the CPAP machine. He smokes thirty cigarettes a day and drinks about sixty grams of ethanol daily. His father died at 55 of a stroke and also had untreated hypertension; there is no pattern of early dementia across generations, and his mother is well at 79. He has never had migraine. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuation and no dream enactment.
